questions.question: When riding in rain or fog, you should:

options.text: Use your high beam headlight.
Use your low beam headlight.
Not use your headlight.
Switch between low and high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlight.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, or fog. High beam headlights reflect off these conditions and make it harder to see.

questions.question: If you lock your rear brake on a good traction surface, you should:

options.text: Let go of the rear brake.
Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: If you lock the rear tire on a good traction surface, keep it locked until you stop. On a surface with good traction, a locked rear wheel will not affect your control as long as the motorcycle stays upright and goes straight.

questions.question: When turning left, you should:

options.text: Press the right handgrip.
Press the left handgrip.
Press both handgrips at the same time.
Not press either handgrip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the left handgrip.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. To make it lean the right way, press the handgrip on the side you want to turn.

questions.question: When passing a row of parked cars, you should:

options.text: Ride on the left side of the lane.
Ride wherever you are most comfortable.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride on the left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of the lane when passing parked cars. This keeps you away from doors opening, people stepping out, and cars pulling out. Always be ready to change position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: When being passed, do not move to the far side of the lane because:

options.text: The passing vehicle may re-enter your lane too early.
You may prevent another vehicle from passing you.
The side closest to the passing vehicle is better.
You are more likely to feel wind from the passing vehicle on the far side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The passing vehicle may re-enter your lane too early.
questions.explanation: Do not ride on the far side of your lane when being passed. This may encourage the other driver to return to your lane before it is safe to do so.

questions.question: If you started a curve on the outside and no traffic is present when exiting, you should move:

options.text: Toward the center of the curve.
Toward the inside of the curve.
Toward the outside of the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the outside of the curve.
questions.explanation: Start on the outside of the curve to see farther ahead and have a wider turning path. Move toward the inside as you turn, then move back toward the outside as you exit. Always adjust your position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, the safest way to approach them is:

options.text: By going straight in your lane.
At a 45-degree angle.
At a 90-degree angle.
At a fast speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: By going straight in your lane.
questions.explanation: Go straight in your lane when crossing angled railroad tracks. Turning to cross at a right angle can be dangerous because it may push you into another lane.

questions.question: How many paths of travel does each traffic lane give a motorcyclist?

options.text: One
Two
Three
Four

questions.correctAnswerText: Three
questions.explanation: Each traffic lane gives motorcyclists three paths of travel: left, center, and right portions of the lane.

questions.question: For routine braking, you should:

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Alternate between front and rear brakes to make them last longer.
Always use both front and rear brakes together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use both front and rear brakes together.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When selecting a helmet, make sure it has all of these qualities, except:

options.text: Meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
Fits snugly.
Has no defects.
Is attractive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is attractive.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation and state standards, fits snugly all the way around, and has no defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve around the dog.
Slow down and let the dog get close. Then speed up and leave it behind.
Park and wait for the dog to lose interest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the dog get close. Then speed up and leave it behind.
questions.explanation: Dogs are often attracted to motorcycles. If chased, slow down and downshift. Let the dog approach. Then accelerate quickly and ride away.

questions.question: How should you brake during a normal motorcycle stop?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a normal stop, apply the front and rear brakes together at the same time. Also downshift.

questions.question: What should you do when braking on a slippery surface?

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both brakes.
Do not use the brakes. Only downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes if you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: What can cause the front wheel and handlebars to shake or wobble?

options.text: Incorrect tire pressure.
Brakes that are not working properly.
A balanced load.
Strong wind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Incorrect tire pressure.
questions.explanation: Most wobbles are caused by improper weight distribution, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: How should you park your motorcycle on the side of the road?

options.text: Park at a 45-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
Park on the sidewalk.
Park at a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
Park at a 90-degree angle with the front wheel touching the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park at a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at a 90-degree angle to the curb. The rear wheel should touch the curb.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop a motorcycle?

options.text: Grab the front brake lever suddenly.
Keep your knees against the gas tank and look ahead.
Apply increasing pressure to the rear brake only.
Use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank and look ahead.
questions.explanation: To stop in a straight line, apply the brakes smoothly and firmly. As you brake, weight moves to the front wheel, giving it more grip. Increase front brake pressure gradually and reduce rear brake pressure. Keep your knees against the gas tank and eyes up to stay straight.

questions.question: In a group of riders, who should set the pace?

options.text: The leader
The riders just behind the leader
The last rider
The oldest rider

questions.correctAnswerText: The last rider
questions.explanation: The last rider should set the pace. This ensures that no riders are left behind.

questions.question: What is the best position to ride in within a lane?

options.text: The left position
The right position
There is no single best position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best position.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. A good rider changes position as conditions change.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are approaching a T intersection.
Your road crosses a divided highway.
You are on an overpass above a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your road crosses a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign means your road crosses a divided highway. A divided highway has two separate one-way roads with a median or guide rail between them.

questions.question: Oil drippings and debris often collect in which part of a lane?

options.text: The left portion
The middle portion
The right portion

questions.correctAnswerText: The middle portion
questions.explanation: Oil drippings and debris from cars and trucks collect in the center of the lane.

questions.question: Motorcycles:

options.text: Need less stopping distance than larger vehicles.
Need the same stopping distance as larger vehicles.
Can stop instantly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need the same stopping distance as larger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Riders must always keep safe distance based on conditions. Motorcycles need the same stopping distance as other vehicles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School zone or school crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zone or school crossing.
questions.explanation: A five-sided yellow or yellow-green sign warns drivers of a school zone or school crossing.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Press the handlebar grip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the handlebar grip opposite the direction you want to turn.
Not hold the grip because it can be dangerous.
Not lean the motorcycle because it is unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handlebar grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: At speeds above a walk, your motorcycle must lean to turn. Pressing the grip in the direction you want to turn will make the motorcycle lean correctly.

questions.question: Which formation is best for a group of riders going through a curve?

options.text: Pyramid
Staggered
Single-file
Compressed

questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is usually best for groups to stay close while each rider keeps safe distance. Use single-file formation for curves, turns, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When riding at night:

options.text: Ride on the road shoulder.
Decrease the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: At night, increase your following distance. Slow down and adjust your lane position as needed.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, you should:

options.text: Keep the wheel locked because it helps you stop faster.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release the front brake right away, then apply it again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks while braking, release the front brake immediately. Then re-apply the brake with gentle, steady pressure.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Stop your motorcycle until the dog loses interest.
Slow down as you approach the dog, then speed up as it gets close.
Swerve around the dog.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you approach the dog, then speed up as it gets close.
questions.explanation: If you see a dog approaching, slow down and downshift as you get close to it. Quickly speed up as the dog approaches.

questions.question: Which protects your eyes from wind?

options.text: Goggles
Windshield
Sunglasses
Eyeglasses

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not provide enough eye protection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
You must turn right.
Watch for traffic on your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right. Do not make a right turn where this sign is posted.

questions.question: If the front wheel locks while braking, you should:

options.text: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again.
Release the front brake right away and use only the rear brake.
Keep the front wheel locked until you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks while braking, release the brake and immediately re-apply it.
